subject: MAP Kickoff — POC acceptance gates & benchmark owners
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: MAP Kickoff — POC acceptance gates & benchmark owners

Elena / team,

Thanks for agreeing to move forward with the POC pilot. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (redwood_MAP_draft_v1.pdf) that outlines the proposed acceptance gates, timeline, and owner assignments. High-level objectives here are to validate:

- Integration & security posture (data flows, KMS)
- Generation quality against clinical prompts (precision / hallucination guardrails)
- Latency & cost under a bounded workload

Proposed acceptance gates (short):
1) Security: SOC2 evidence + network design sign-off
2) Quality: benchmark suite—3 clinical prompt sets with pass thresholds
3) Ops: end-to-end latency P95 < 1.2s for 512-token median workload
4) Business: stakeholder acceptance and go/no-go sign-off meeting

Can you confirm the primary internal owners on your side? We suggest Jorge Rivera as your PM and Elena as clinical owner. On our side I’ve included Marcus (benchmarks) and Neha (security/compliance). I’ll own coordination and the MAP cadence.

Immediate asks:
- Please review the attached MAP and the quick benchmark plan in the doc (high-level)
- Confirm Jorge’s email (cc if helpful) and who will own the prompt curation on your side
- Any hard constraints on a target decision date (we were aiming for the week of Dec 13)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short SOW/DocuSign pointer once we lock owners and acceptance gates.

—
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Tessa — thanks for the clear summary and the MAP draft. Jorge and I reviewed and we broadly agree with the gates. A few notes from Clearwell:

- Jorge (copied) will be the program owner for timelines and stakeholder orchestration.
- Clinical prompt ownership will be split between Elena (clinical SME) and Jorge (product). We’ll own prompt validation and labelling.
- SOC2 evidence: we can provide our latest SOC2 report and a short network diagram by Nov 30.

We attached our compliance questions workbook — some of the items will need a short follow-up with your security team.

Preferred decision date: Dec 17 (end of week) — that gives our clinical reviewers two weeks after your benchmark run to sign off.

Elena

Elena / all — quick note on the benchmark and owner recommendations from the engineering side. Thanks Tessa for the draft. I pulled together a short harness outline (benchmark_harness_v1.md) and a proposed measurement plan:

Benchmark plan (summary):
- Prompt sets: 3 clinical tracks (Intake, Differential, Discharge) — ~120 canonical prompts each.
- Metrics: accuracy/recall against annotated gold, hallucination rate (human-labeled), response coherence score, latency P95.
- Pass thresholds: accuracy >= 92% aggregated, hallucination rate <= 3% across prompts, latency P95 < 1.2s (512 tokens).
- Test harness: run using Redwood Optimize with KV caching off/on to baseline costs. We’ll provide raw outputs + trace logs for your clinical review.

Owners (Redwood):
- Prompt engineering & bench design: Marcus Lin
- Security & compliance coordination: Neha Kapoor
- Prompt-level quality assessments & eval tooling: Rishi Malhotra

Suggested schedule:
- Nov 30: exchange final prompt list + SOC2 report
- Dec 6–9: run first benchmark pass (engineering)
- Dec 10–14: clinical review window
- Dec 15–17: go/no-go decision meeting (target Dec 17)

I’ll link the harness and include example output rows in the shared folder once Jorge confirms S3 access.

—
Marcus Lin
Senior ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
